# Ten Lectures on Integral Lattices

## Lecture Notes

## 1 Lattices

Definition 1. A lattice is a free Z-module L of finite rank with a symmetric bilinear form b : $L \times L \to \mathbb { Q }$ . It is integral if $b ( L , L ) \subseteq \mathbb { Z } .$

## 2 Gram matrices

For a basis $e _ { 1 } , \ldots , e _ { n }$ of L the Gram matrix is $G = ( b ( e _ { i } , e _ { j } ) ) _ { i , j }$ , and

$$
\det L = \det G.
$$

A change of basis by $P \in \operatorname { G L } _ { n } ( \mathbb { Z } )$ replaces G by $P ^ { T } G P$

## 3 Dual lattices

The dual lattice is $L ^ { \vee } = \{ x \in L \otimes \mathbb { Q } : b ( x , L ) \subseteq \mathbb { Z } \}$ . For integral L we have $L \subseteq L ^ { \vee }$ and $[ L ^ { \vee } : L ] = | \operatorname* { d e i } L |$

## 4 Discriminant forms

For an even lattice the discriminant group $A _ { L } = L ^ { \vee } / L$ carries the quadratic form

$$
q _ {L} (x + L) = \frac {1}{2} b (x, x) \bmod \mathbb {Z}.
$$

## 5 Root lattices

The root lattice $A _ { n }$ $\textstyle \left\{ x \in \mathbb { Z } ^ { n + 1 } : \sum _ { i } x _ { i } = 0 \right\}$ , with det $A _ { n } = n + 1$ . The lattice $D _ { n }$ is $\left\{ x \in \mathbb { Z } ^ { n } : \sum _ { i } x _ { i } \equiv 0 { \pmod { 2 } } \right\}$

## 6 The lattice $E _ { 8 }$

Theorem 1. ${ \cal E } _ { 8 } = D _ { 8 } \cup ( D _ { 8 } + { \textstyle \frac { 1 } { 2 } } ( 1 , . . . , 1 ) )$ is the unique even unimodular positive definite lattice of rank 8, and it has 240 roots.

## 7 Theta series

$$
\theta_ {E _ {8}} (q) = 1 + 2 4 0 \sum_ {n \geq 1} \sigma_ {3} (n) q ^ {n}.
$$

The theta series of a positive definite lattice is $\begin{array} { r } { \theta _ { L } ( q ) = \sum _ { x \in L } q ^ { b ( x , x ) / 2 } } \end{array}$ . For $E _ { 8 }$

## 8 Genus

Two lattices are in the same genus if $L \otimes \mathbb { Z } _ { p } \cong M \otimes \mathbb { Z } _ { p }$ for every prime p and $L \otimes \mathbb { R } \cong M \otimes \mathbb { R }$

## 9 The mass formula

The Smith–Minkowski–Siegel mass formula states

$$
\sum_ {M \in \mathrm{gen} (L)} \frac {1}{| \mathrm{O} (M) |} = \mathrm{mass} (L).
$$

## 10 Niemeier lattices

There are exactly 24 even unimodular positive definite lattices of rank 24; the Leech lattice is the only one without roots.
